# Academic plots

## Demographics

```{r demographics, results='asis'}
demographic_plots = list()
for (question in demographics) {
  counts = demographic_counts[[question]]
  p = category_plot(
    counts, question_title(question),

    response_order = response_orders[[question]]
  )
  demographic_plots[[question]] = p
  show_survey_plot(p, name = paste0("demographics-", question))
}
```

## AI change

```{r ai-change, results='asis'}
change_plot = category_plot(
  change_counts, question_title("change"),

  response_order = response_orders$change, participants = nrow(change_respondents),
  note = paste(
    "Multiple selections allowed; percentages can sum to more than 100%.",
    "Training fewer researchers excludes PhD students.",
    "Responses with conflicting selections are excluded from this question."
  )
)
show_survey_plot(change_plot, name = "ai-change-bars")
```

## AI questions by discipline

```{r ai-by-discipline, results='asis'}
for (question in ai_questions) {
  p = grouped_ai_plot(data_filtered, question, "discipline_of_interest",
                      discipline_order,
                      rank_responses = discipline_rank_responses[[question]],
                      hierarchy_parent = "Natural sciences")
  grouped_plots[[paste0("discipline_", question)]] = p
  show_survey_plot(p)
}
```


## AI questions by subfield within disciplines

Each set compares the lower-level fields within one primary discipline. The
All respondents bar pools valid answers within that discipline, including
respondents who did not specify a subfield. Named subfields with fewer than 10
respondents are pooled into the corresponding Other category before calculating percentages.

```{r ai-by-subfield, results='asis'}
for (discipline in names(subfield_disciplines)) {
  parent = subfield_disciplines[[discipline]]
  cat("\n\n### ", parent, "\n\n", sep = "")
  discipline_data = subfield_data[[discipline]]$data
  subfield_order = subfield_data[[discipline]]$order

  for (question in ai_questions) {
    p = grouped_ai_plot(discipline_data, question, "discipline_2", subfield_order,
                        rank_responses = discipline_rank_responses[[question]])
    if (is.null(p)) next
    p = p + labs(x = "Share of respondents within each subfield")
    row_labels = p$data |> distinct(group, y) |> arrange(y) |> pull(group)
    y_scale = p$scales$get_scales("y")
    y_scale$labels = stringr::str_wrap(recode(row_labels, !!!subfield_labels), width = 31)
    name = paste("grouped", discipline, "subfields", question, sep = "_")
    attr(p, "figure_label") = name
    grouped_plots[[name]] = p
    show_survey_plot(p)
  }
}
```

## AI questions by career stage

```{r ai-by-stage, results='asis'}
for (question in ai_questions) {
  p = grouped_ai_plot(data_filtered, question, "stage", response_orders$stage,
                      fixed_order = TRUE)
  grouped_plots[[paste0("stage_", question)]] = p
  show_survey_plot(p)
}
```


## AI questions by country group

Groups are USA, the 27 EU member states plus the UK, China (ISO3 CHN), India,
and Other countries. All remaining identified countries are included in Other
countries; missing countries are excluded.
Agreement plots rank groups by strongly agree; awareness ranks by very familiar.

```{r ai-by-country-group, results='asis'}
for (question in ai_questions) {
  p = grouped_ai_plot(data_filtered, question, "country_group", country_group_order,
                      rank_responses = discipline_rank_responses[[question]])
  grouped_plots[[paste0("country_group_", question)]] = p
  show_survey_plot(p)
}
```

## AI questions by familiarity, dichotomized

```{r ai-by-familiarity, results='asis'}
for (question in setdiff(ai_questions, "awareness")) {
  p = grouped_ai_plot(data_filtered, question, "awareness_dichotomized",
                      c("Not familiar", "Familiar"), fixed_order = TRUE)
  grouped_plots[[paste0("familiarity_", question)]] = p
  show_survey_plot(p)
}
```
